newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end firmer after routine session.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end firmer after routine session.

text.p: FCOJ futures closed firmer on Tuesday after a routine session with a good portion of the day's activity devoted to completing the rollover from March to May, traders said.

A broker noted some speculative buying along with local shortcovering which pushed up the market to a high of 82.20 cents per pound, before slipping back to close at 81.85 cents in the most active May contract, up 0.15 cent.
Volume was good at an estimated 4,500 lots due to the rollover. Monday's official volume was 5,958 lots.

The spec/hedge report from NYCE indicated that speculators were 62.80 percent long at close on Friday, up from 60.30 percent in the previous week. The change was not considered big enough to have had any major impact on the market.

Meanwhile U.S. production of orange juice should increase during the next few years as maturing trees come into full production, the U.S. Dept of Agriculture said in a report on horticulture released Tuesday.
Better quality oranges grown in Florida may lead to a rise in the percentage of the crop sold for fresh market. Most of the current Florida crop is processed, the report added.
Florida is already heading for a record crop in 1996/97.
